clue.text: Our price is smashing — one can rake in the money

definitions.text: one can rake in the money

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words up, so the letters of 'Our price' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop boasts that its prices are smashing, while someone else pockets the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is smashing' signals rearranging the letters of OUR PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino employee rakes gamblers' chips across the table, collecting and paying out money.

clue.text: Plant left half cut under pile of straw

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the short piece below the heap

parts.note: a cock, as in haycock, is a heap of hay or straw

indicators.note: cutting the word in half keeps its first two letters

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant is left half-trimmed beneath a heap of straw.
explanation.walkthrough: A haycock is the conical heap of hay or straw once built in fields; in a down clue 'under' means the trimmed word sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncockle is a weed of cornfields, often just called by this shorter name.

clue.text: Gaping fish go up to the top

indicators.note: the reversed word goes at the top of the down entry
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish rises to the surface with its mouth open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaping' here means staring open-mouthed, not hanging open, so the fish's mouth in the surface is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling is staring at someone admiringly or lecherously, much like gawping.

clue.text: Mineral containing carbon found in unvarnished ceramic

indicators.note: found in puts the combined mineral piece inside the word for unvarnished

parts.note: plain means unadorned or unvarnished

indicators.note: containing has the mineral hold the carbon symbol

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A geologist identifies a carbon-bearing mineral in an unglazed pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine white china, a type of ceramic ware.

clue.text: Additional account given in exuberant mammer

parts.note: extra means additional
a version is an account of events

explanation.surface: A second story is told with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'mammer', a misprint for 'manner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing, sociable behaviour is the personality trait of an extravert.

clue.text: Small bits of dirt in cable reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for cable is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: flex is an electrical cable

explanation.surface: Specks of grime are found in some wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Specks or spots of dirt are tiny particles scattered over a surface.

clue.text: See copper on motorway — he may be passing through on a job

definitions.text: he may be passing through on a job

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
CU is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A traffic policeman watches a motorway where travellers pass through on business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in doctor or cleric covers a post temporarily before moving on.

clue.text: Notes little brat with matches

parts.note: a chit is a cheeky young girl
ties are drawn matches, or contests in a cup

explanation.surface: A naughty child is playing with matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Chits are short written notes or vouchers, often recording a debt.

clue.text: The month after summer hols a class may be different

parts.note: September, abbreviated Sep, follows the school summer holidays
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: After the summer break a school class may have changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate means distinct or apart from others.

clue.text: Speed gets someone well-known bowled out

indicators.note: out says a letter is left out of the famous person

parts.note: a celebrity is someone famous
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A famous cricketer is bowled out quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or quickness.

clue.text: Economise, using fabric with minimum of pleating

parts.note: scrim is a coarse open-weave cotton or linen fabric

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A dressmaker saves money by using cheap cloth and few pleats.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be sparing or thrifty with money.

clue.text: Garden plant's quality improved

parts.note: a standard is a level of quality
rose means went up or improved

explanation.surface: A gardener says the quality of a plant has got better.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bush grafted onto a tall single stem is a familiar garden shrub.

clue.text: Caught in country road — puncture

indicators.note: in puts the letter for caught inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a rural road with a punctured tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or cut open, as a doctor does a boil.

clue.text: Type of instrument showing change around the hour

indicators.note: around has the word for change wrapped about the hour

parts.note: to alter is to change
the hour is a time

explanation.surface: A clock-like instrument shows a change around the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is an aircraft instrument measuring height.

clue.text: Manage to complete the circle?

definitions.meaning: to get by financially, scraping through
a circle is complete when its two ends join up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having just enough money to cover one's expenses.

clue.text: Insect — it's excited studier of nature

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A naturalist finds an insect that is agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher of the natural world works in the sciences.

clue.text: Date ship at sea entered anchorage

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship's arrival date at harbour is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges DATE SHIP. Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth used by the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait off the south English coast where fleets famously anchor for reviews.

clue.text: University of solid worth, from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means the word is judged by sound, not spelling

parts.note: sterling means of solid, excellent worth

explanation.surface: Gossip about a university's excellent reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirling is a Scottish university town.
explanation.definitionFit: A university in central Scotland takes the name of its town.

clue.text: Meddle and give an indication of wanting to row?

definitions.text: give an indication of wanting to row?
definitions.meaning: taking up an oar literally, as a rower about to row would

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means interfering uninvited in someone else's business.

clue.text: Game or beef?

definitions.meaning: a beef is a complaint or grumble

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a game bird and a slang complaint.

clue.text: Eastern scholar criticised the thing audibly

indicators.note: audibly means spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: panned it means slated it, criticised it

explanation.surface: A learned man from the East was scathing about something, out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is a learned Hindu teacher or wise man in India.

clue.text: In the beginning, the Lord erupts without silence!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the call for silence
something that erupts bursts apart, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A biblical image: at the dawn of creation, God bursts forth noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the' is a link; 'erupts' rearranges THE LORD into THREOLD, which 'without' wraps around SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the point of entry or start of something, as on the brink of a career.

clue.text: Sap's first appearing on tree, gluey stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the letter above the tree
first takes just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a lime is a linden tree

explanation.surface: Sticky sap oozes from a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is any viscous, sticky substance.

clue.text: A male, boy? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse means the pieces are written back to front

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about a man and a boy, then asking for the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' reads AMRON backwards; the whole clue also defines, since the opposite of a male boy is a girl, and this is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, the reverse sex of a boy, built backwards from the pieces.

clue.text: English legal extract

parts.note: licit means lawful

explanation.surface: An excerpt from an English law text.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out a response or information from someone is a verb sense of extract.

clue.text: Bone in old burial site, near the end

indicators.note: in places the bone inside the burial site

parts.note: a mound, or barrow, was an ancient burial place
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find a bone in an ancient barrow, close to the end of a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dying or in terminal decline is about to finish.

clue.text: Weapon's untidy ends switched

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word swap places

parts.note: ragged means scruffy or untidy

explanation.surface: A soldier's weapon is in a shabby state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends switched' swaps the R and D of RAGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stabbing knife is a classic weapon.

clue.text: Despatched to one hospital department not anaesthetised?

parts.note: sent means despatched
I is the Roman numeral for one
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A patient is sent to a hospital ward, wondering if they will be put under.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is conscious and able to feel, unlike a patient under anaesthetic.
